English review:

I recommend it, but with some important reservations.

I will be very honest: my review is positive because I do not want to judge the game unfairly, since I was not able to play it as much as I wanted. The game seems very good for people who can properly get into it and enjoy its style.

One thing I really liked was the visual presentation. The graphics, the map design, and the overall realistic atmosphere are very well done. The maps feel detailed and believable, and that was one of the parts that impressed me the most.

However, there are some points that made it very difficult for me to actually enjoy the game. The first one is related to connection and hosting. If your internet provider uses NAT or CGNAT, or if your router configuration is limited, hosting a server or playing with friends can become complicated. For some players this may not be a problem, but depending on your internet setup, the multiplayer experience can be frustrating.

Another point is the server system itself. Personally, I do not really like games where you need to search for servers, join specific communities, deal with different setups, mods, rules, and configurations. I understand that this can be a positive thing for many players, because Arma 3 offers a huge amount of freedom and customization. But for me, this ended up feeling more like a barrier than a benefit.

Because of these connection and server-related issues, I was not able to have a great experience with the game. Still, I can clearly see why many people consider Arma 3 an excellent game.

It is also important to say that this is not a simple action shooter. Arma 3 is a very tactical military game. It is very different from something like Call of Duty. Here, roles matter a lot: if you are a sniper, a pilot, a soldie…

I will still recommend this game for audiences who are willing to buy DLCs for additional missions and story.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the controls and interface as overly complicated, clunky, and difficult to learn.

citations.review_text:
Not Recommended

I really wanted to enjoy Arma III, but it just wasn't for me.

The game is incredibly complicated, with a steep learning curve that makes even basic tasks feel overwhelming. Instead of easing new players in, it often feels like you're expected to already know everything.

It also feels surprisingly lonely. Unless you already have friends who play or you're willing to join a dedicated community, the experience can feel empty and disconnected. The sandbox is impressive, but it doesn't do much to help solo newcomers find their footing.

There's no denying the depth and realism, and I can see why long-time fans love it. But if you're looking for a beginner-friendly military shooter, this probably isn't it.

Arma 3 remains in 2026 one of the most complete military sandbox simulations ever released. It focuses on large scale combined arms warfare where infantry, vehicles, air support, and logistics all interact in a realistic way. The emphasis is less on fast action and more on coordination, tactics, and immersion.

From a modern access media perspective, most of the game’s longevity comes from its community. Mods and community servers effectively turn Arma 3 into multiple different experiences, ranging from modern military operations to survival scenarios and total conversion campaigns. Organized milsim groups are still a major part of how the game is played today.

The downside is its age. The interface is complex, onboarding is difficult for new players, and performance can still struggle in large missions. AI behavior is also inconsistent at times.

Overall, Arma 3 in 2026 is more of a military simulation platform than a traditional shooter. It still offers unmatched depth and scale if you are willing to invest the time to learn it or play with community groups.

**Arma 3** is one of the most realistic military simulation games I have ever played. The scale of the battles, the detailed mechanics, and the freedom the game offers make every mission feel unique. Whether you're fighting as infantry, driving armored vehicles, flying helicopters, or coordinating with a squad, the game delivers an experience that few military shooters can match.

One of the things I enjoy most is the incredible freedom. There are countless scenarios, community-made missions, and mods that add new maps, weapons, vehicles, and gameplay mechanics. The Steam Workshop alone provides enough content to keep you playing for hundreds or even thousands of hours.

However, I have to be honest: **when I first started playing, I had absolutely no idea what I was doing.** The game has a very steep learning curve. There are so many controls, mechanics, and systems that beginners can easily feel overwhelmed. It definitely takes patience before everything starts to make sense.

Once you learn the basics, though, the game becomes incredibly rewarding. Working together with teammates, planning operations, communicating effectively, and successfully completing difficult missions provide a level of satisfaction that very few games can offer.

Overall, Arma 3 is an outstanding military sandbox with unmatched realism and endless replayability. It's not beginner-friendly, but if you're willing to invest the time to learn it, you'll discover one of the best military simulation games ever made.

I have thousands of hours in DayZ and Arma Reforger, Arma 2 and the original Operation Flashpoint games. I'm an enjoyer of tactical shooters, and I've played Squad and Project Reality probably even more than all of the previous games combined.
Yet somehow I never got Arma 3. So I did now, because I was sick of Arma Reforger crashing and disconnecting me from servers.
Long story short: I know it's an old game, but I got it just now, so I'll treat it as a new game.

I don't really care about graphics... It looks ok, DayZ looks better.. which is weird since it was an Arma 3 mod. 
It has the most convoluted idiotic pile of keybinds that I've ever seen in my life... I've played a ton of games that are complex, but they all try not to be complicated.. But dudes, ARMA 3 HAS SPACE SET AS IT'S INTERACTION KEY... Like what in the world is that????
It gets worse though. The moment you log in you are greeted with a FOV of 70. If you're like me - you'll get sick. So I tried changing that and the mouse sensitivity.. The sensitivity has 2 sliders.. horizontal and vertical. None of them display any numbers, and the only thing you can do is eyeball it and hope for the best.. Good luck trying to match them.
Then I went back looking for the FOV slider.. Took me a while to realize that there isn't one. So I googled it. And you apparently need to "hack" the game files if you don't like vomiting on your keyboard.. 
And for that, you OBVIOUSLY need to use one of the 30 million Arma 3 FOV calculators found on google. So I tried 10 to 20 different ones. AND ALL OF THEM GAVE ME DIFFERENT RESULTS (or the numbers I had to copy and paste into the game files), AND NOT A SINGLE ONE WAS CORRECT. I'm using a standard ultrawide monitor, I gave each and every one of those calculators the same input, and each of them gave me a different output lol
The game either looked stretched horizontally, or vertically.. In some cases even the game menu fell apart when I changed some of the settings. 
I…

citations.review_text: This game is great. I got it just for the Antistasi mod and had a great time. If you don't mind the AI being silly at times and a slightly dated engine, It's a good buy when on sale. Runs perfectly fine on my laptop, though I never really touched the graphics settings.

it does have issues though, it can stutter and takes a lot of gpu, it has a lot of graphical bugs that have not been fixed, and the game is old enough it is not looking like they are going too. there are several physics bugs that can make it so that you just end up under the floor sometimes or so that you are softlocked, but, those are pretty rare. there are many bugs when it comes to long range sniping (what I do), your bullets can sometimes just go through someone without hitting them, sometimes the ground can be super buggy, resulting in people just being in the ground so you cant see them, spotting mechanics can be buggy, the distance finder can bug out sometimes and give you bad readings, and sniping also almost completely needs the marksmen dlc. it really sucks that they made so much of the game behind a pay wall, when you already paid for the game. so add the price of whatever dlc would need to play the game how you want to to the total you want to pay for it. so wait for it to be on sale

After more than 4,000 hours in Arma 3, I think it's safe to say this game has earned its place as one of my all-time favourites.

Arma 3 isn't a game you can judge after a few hours. It's a military sandbox that rewards patience, teamwork and learning. The scale of the battles, the freedom to approach missions in different ways, and the endless amount of community-made content mean there's always something new to experience.

For me, the biggest reason to keep coming back is the online team play. There's nothing quite like being part of a well-organised squad where communication, coordination and planning all come together. Whether it's a small co-op mission or a large-scale operation with dozens of players, the moments you create with your teammates are unforgettable.

The modding community deserves huge credit too. Mods have kept the game feeling fresh for years and have added an incredible amount of content and realism.

It's not perfect—there's definitely a learning curve, and the occasional bug or clunky moment is part of the Arma experience—but if you're willing to invest the time, few games offer this level of immersion and teamwork.

4,000+ hours played, and I still find myself coming back for "just one more mission." That probably says everything.
The game is a all round great game, can be difficult for beginner players as it is overwhelming, but once you play for a while and learn more it becomes a very fun and imersive game
